blocks.text: Population geography studies **how people are spread and how they move**. Andhra Pradesh (post-2014, ~**4.9 crore**, ~5th-largest state) shows an **uneven distribution** — dense, fertile **coastal deltas** versus sparse, dry **Rayalaseema and Eastern-Ghat tracts** — shaped by **water, soil, urbanisation and migration**. Its **moderate density**, ageing profile and out-migration are the defining demographic-geographic facts.

rows: United AP ~8.46 cr; **residuary AP ~4.94 cr** (~5th largest); moderate growth (~9-11% decadal, falling).
~**308/km²** (residuary AP) — below the national average; densest in **coastal deltaic districts (Krishna, W. Godavari)**, sparse in **Rayalaseema & agency areas**.
**Coastal Andhra** most populous; **Rayalaseema** least; a **river-and-fertility-driven** pattern.
**Rural→urban** migration to Hyderabad (pre-2014), Bengaluru, Chennai, Vizag; seasonal & Gulf (esp. from Rayalaseema/Godavari) migration.

items: **Physical determinants of distribution**: **water availability and soil fertility** dominate — the **irrigated Godavari-Krishna deltas** carry the densest rural populations, while **arid Rayalaseema and forested Eastern-Ghat agency areas** are sparse; relief and rainfall (G-074) map directly onto density.

**Population movements**: AP is a **net out-migration** state — **rural-to-urban** flows to Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada-Guntur (the capital region) and (historically) Hyderabad; **inter-state** flows to Bengaluru/Chennai/Hyderabad; and notable **international (Gulf) migration** from Rayalaseema and coastal districts (remittances).

**Urbanisation pattern**: ~**30% urban**; a few large centres (Visakhapatnam the largest city, Vijayawada-Guntur conurbation, Tirupati, Nellore, Kurnool) with the **Amaravati capital region** planned as a new growth pole; bifurcation removed Hyderabad, reshaping urban geography.

**Demographic transition**: AP is **relatively advanced in the transition** — low fertility (below replacement), **an ageing population** and slowing growth — with policy implications (labour, elderly care) explored in G-084.

sections.heading: Demographics — age, sex, rural & urban composition

blocks.text: The **composition** of AP's population — its **age structure, sex ratio, and rural-urban split** — reveals a state in **advanced demographic transition**: a **favourable-but-narrowing working-age share, an ageing tendency, a broadly balanced (even female-surplus) sex ratio, and a still-majority-rural but urbanising society** — the human-resource profile that shapes AP's development choices.

rows: ~**993–997** (favourable, near or above the national ~943) — coastal districts high; a relatively **women-balanced** state.
Falling child (0-6) share; large working-age cohort (demographic dividend) but **rising elderly share** — AP ageing faster than most states.
~**70% rural / 30% urban**; urbanising steadily; concentrated in a few cities.
~**67%** (below national); male-female and rural-urban gaps persist.

sections.heading: Composition, dividend and the ageing challenge

items: **Sex composition (a bright spot)**: AP's **sex ratio (~996) is among India's better**, near/above unity, with a favourable child sex ratio relative to the north — reflecting the southern demographic pattern; but selective concerns persist in pockets.

**Age structure & the dividend**: a **large working-age population** offers a **demographic dividend**, but AP's **low fertility means the window is closing and the elderly share rising** — an **'ageing before rich' risk** demanding skilling, jobs and elderly-care policy now.

**Rural-urban composition**: still **~70% rural** (agriculture-dependent), yet **urbanising** around Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada-Guntur (capital region), Tirupati and Nellore; managing **balanced urbanisation** (avoiding one mega-city) is a planning goal, sharpened by the loss of Hyderabad.

**Human-capital dimension**: **literacy ~67%** (below national) with gender/rural gaps; improving **education, skilling and health** is essential to convert the demographic profile into a dividend — the core policy takeaway.

sections.heading: Social groups — race, caste, tribe, religion & linguistic groups

blocks.text: AP's society is a **plural mosaic** of **castes, tribes, religions and linguistic communities**, overwhelmingly **Telugu-speaking and Hindu-majority**, with significant **SC, ST, OBC, Muslim and Christian** populations. Understanding this social composition — its **caste structure, tribal (agency) communities, and religio-linguistic makeup** — is essential to AP's politics, welfare policy and social geography.

rows: **OBCs** the largest bloc; **SCs ~17%** (Malas, Madigas — the influential Mala-Madiga categorisation issue); dominant landed castes (Kamma, Reddy, Kapu) shape politics.
**~5-6%**; Eastern-Ghat 'agency' tribes — **Koya, Konda Reddi, Savara, Chenchu, Yanadi, Yerukula, Sugalis/Lambadas**; PVTGs (Chenchu, Bondo-linked).
**Telugu** overwhelming majority; **Urdu** (largest minority language), Tamil/Kannada/Odia border-region minorities, tribal languages (Koya, Savara).

items: **On 'race'**: modern anthropology rejects rigid racial typologies; India/AP populations are a **deep intermixture** — the older classification (Caucasoid/Australoid/etc.) is only of historical interest, with tribal groups often linked to **proto-Australoid** strands; present 'race' cautiously as an outdated frame.

**Caste structure & mobilisation**: **OBCs form the largest segment**; **SCs (~17%, chiefly Malas & Madigas)** — the **SC sub-categorisation (Madiga/MRPS) demand** is a live AP issue; **dominant peasant castes (Kamma, Reddy, Kapu, Velama)** and the **Kapu-reservation agitation** shape state politics.

**Tribal communities (agency areas)**: STs (~5-6%) inhabit the **Eastern-Ghat agency** — **Koya, Konda Reddi, Savara, Chenchu (PVTG), Yanadi, Yerukula, Sugalis/Lambadas** — governed under the **Fifth Schedule/PESA/FRA**, with distinct languages, podu cultivation and welfare needs.

**Religio-linguistic pluralism**: a **Hindu-majority, Telugu-speaking** society with a substantial **Muslim (Urdu) minority** (a Qutb-Shahi cultural legacy — HCOA-053) and a notable **Christian** presence (missionary legacy — HCOI-026); this plurality underpins AP's composite culture and its welfare/minority policy.

blocks.text: **Urban migration** — the movement of people from villages and small towns to cities — is reshaping AP's society, driven by **jobs, education and services**. Coupled with the state's **educational characteristics** (moderate literacy, a strong professional-education base but persistent gaps), migration and education together determine AP's **human-capital trajectory** and the success of its demographic dividend.

rows: **Employment (industry/services), education, better amenities**; distress-push from drought (Rayalaseema) & farm stress; historic pull of Hyderabad, now Vizag/Vijayawada, Bengaluru, Chennai.
**Rural→urban, small-town→city, inter-state, and international (Gulf)**; also student migration for higher/professional education.
Literacy ~**67%**; strong **engineering/medical private-college** sector; but rural-urban & gender gaps, quality & dropout concerns.
Urban growth & slums, remittances & rural transformation, brain-drain of skilled youth, but also skill-upgrading and social mobility.

items: **Why they migrate**: **economic pull (jobs, higher wages, services) and push (agrarian distress, drought, landlessness — acute in Rayalaseema)**; **educational migration** (students to cities/other states for professional courses) is a distinct, growing stream.

**Educational characteristics**: AP has a **large private professional-education sector (engineering, medicine, pharmacy)** and schemes like **fee reimbursement**, but faces **moderate literacy (~67%), rural-urban and gender disparities, learning-outcome/quality gaps and dropout** — the education deficit that migration both reflects and reinforces.

**Consequences of urban migration**: **city growth and slum/informal-settlement pressures, strain on urban services, remittance-led rural change, and skilled-youth out-migration (brain drain)** to Bengaluru/Hyderabad/abroad — a two-edged process.

**Policy response**: **balanced urbanisation (avoiding one mega-city), skilling missions, improving school quality & retention, decentralised job creation (industrial corridors, capital region), and managing migrant welfare** — converting migration-plus-education into the demographic dividend (G-084).

sections.heading: Fauna — wild animals, birds, reptiles & mammals of AP

blocks.text: Andhra Pradesh's **fauna** is rich and varied — from **tigers and leopards of the Nallamala** to **the Godavari-Krishna estuarine crocodiles and Olive Ridley turtles**, and the vast **bird congregations of Kolleru and Pulicat**. Protected through a network of **tiger reserves, national parks and sanctuaries**, AP's wildlife is a key ecological asset of the Eastern Ghats and its coast.

rows: **Tiger & leopard (Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve, Nallamala)**, sloth bear, Indian wolf, blackbuck, chital, sambar, **fishing cat (Coringa)**, Indian pangolin.
**Pelicans, painted storks, flamingos (Pulicat, Nelapattu, Kolleru)**; migratory waterfowl; the **Telineelapuram/Telukunchi Siberian-crane-and-pelican sites**.
**Mugger & estuarine crocodiles (Coringa, Godavari), Indian python, king cobra, monitor lizards; Olive Ridley sea turtles** nesting on the coast.
**Tiger, Olive Ridley turtle, Indian pangolin, fishing cat, grey slender loris, Jerdon's courser (rediscovered in AP)**.

items: **Flagship — the tiger**: the **Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve (India's largest)** in the Nallamala anchors AP's big-cat and prey conservation (tiger, leopard, sloth bear, the Chenchu tribe within).

**Coastal & wetland fauna**: **Coringa (mangrove — crocodiles, fishing cat, otters), Kolleru (freshwater — pelicans/storks), Pulicat & Nelapattu (flamingos, pelicans)** host spectacular birdlife; the **coast is an Olive Ridley turtle nesting ground** (arribada-linked conservation).

**The Jerdon's courser story**: this **critically endangered bird, thought extinct, was rediscovered in the Sri Lankamaleswara sanctuary (Cuddapah, 1986)** — a celebrated AP conservation landmark and a threatened-species emblem.

**Protected-area network & threats**: AP's **national parks (Papikonda, Sri Venkateswara, Rajiv Gandhi/ Rollapadu-blackbuck), sanctuaries (Coringa, Kolleru, Nelapattu, Pulicat, Rollapadu-great Indian bustard-linked)** protect this fauna against **habitat loss, poaching, red-sanders/mining pressure and wetland shrinkage**.

sections.heading: Flora — trees & plants of Andhra Pradesh

blocks.text: AP's **flora** mirrors its rainfall gradient (G-078) — from **mangroves and deltaic vegetation on the coast, through moist and dry deciduous forests of the Eastern Ghats, to thorn-scrub in arid Rayalaseema**. It is distinguished by **endemic and economically prized species — red sanders, sandalwood, teak and a rich medicinal-plant flora** — making the Eastern Ghats a notable centre of plant diversity.

rows: **Avicennia, Rhizophora (Coringa mangroves)**, casuarina plantations, palmyra, coconut.
**Teak, terminalia, rosewood, bamboo**; the richest forest belt (Araku, Nallamala).
**Red sanders (endemic), sandalwood, hardwickia, acacia, neem**; degraded to thorn scrub in Rayalaseema.
**Red sanders, sandalwood, bamboo, cashew, medicinal herbs (from the Tirumala/Seshachalam & Maredumilli forests)**.

items: **Endemic flagship — red sanders**: **Pterocarpus santalinus**, endemic to the **Seshachalam-Palakonda hills** of Rayalaseema, is AP's most famous plant — prized for its wood, **CITES-protected**, and the target of notorious smuggling; its conservation is a signature AP issue.

**Economic flora**: **teak, rosewood, bamboo (paper/craft), sandalwood, cashew, casuarina** and vast **medicinal-plant** wealth support industry and tribal livelihoods (NTFPs — G-079); the Eastern Ghats are a reservoir of wild crop relatives and ethnobotanical species.

**Vegetation-rainfall link**: flora grades with rainfall — **mangroves & casuarina on the wet coast, teak-bamboo moist-deciduous forests in the Ghats, and red-sanders/sandal dry-deciduous-to-thorn scrub in arid Rayalaseema** — a textbook rainfall-controlled sequence.

**Conservation framework & threats**: **biosphere reserves (Seshachalam), sacred groves, sanctuaries and afforestation** protect AP flora against **podu cultivation, red-sanders smuggling, mining, fire and invasive species (Lantana, Prosopis)** — sustainable forest management and community stewardship are the response.
